Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

The inbox is getting busy. Let staff mark tickets `normal` or `high` priority; default to normal.
Add priority to the existing ticket responses and updates, and let staff combine filters:

```http
GET /api/v1/tickets?status=open&assignee_id=unassigned&priority=high&q=receipt
```

Support status, assignee, requester, and priority filters, plus `q` for a case-insensitive search
through subjects and public comments. Use `assignee_id` and `requester_id` for people; `unassigned`
means nobody is assigned. Search should treat what the user types as literal text.
Customers can filter their own requests by status. Priority is internal.

require "digest"

class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze
  EXPIRATION_WINDOW = 7.days

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :sent_invitations, optional: true
  belongs_to :accepted_by, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :accepted_invitations, optional: true

  normalizes :role, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :role, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ROLES }

  validates :sent_at, presence: true
  validates :expires_at, presence: true
  validate :associations_belong_to_account
  validate :email_not_already_taken_or_invited, on: :create

  scope :ordered, -> { order(id: :asc) }
  scope :pending_at, ->(now = Time.current) { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at > ?", now) }
  scope :accepted, -> { where.not(accepted_at: nil) }
  scope :revoked, -> { where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil) }
  scope :expired_at, ->(now = Time.current) { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at <= ?", now) }

  def self.with_status(status, now = Time.current)
    case status
    when "pending" then pending_at(now)
    when "accepted" then accepted
    when "revoked" then revoked
    when "expired" then expired_at(now)
    else none
    end
  end

  def self.digest_token(raw_token)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token.to_s)
  end

  def self.find_by_token(raw_token)
    return nil if raw_token.blank?

    find_by(token_digest: digest_token(raw_token))
  end

    raw_token = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)

  end

    if accepted_at.present?
      "accepted"
    elsif revoked_at.present?
      "revoked"
    elsif expires_at <= now

    post "/api/v1/registrations",
      params: {
        user: {
          name: name,
          email: email,
          password: password
        }
      },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
      as: :json
    assert_response :created

    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    token = extract_token_from_mail(mail, expected_path: "/verify-email", expected_account: subdomain.downcase)

    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
      params: { email_verification: { token: token } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    account = Account.find_by!(subdomain: subdomain.downcase)
    User.find_by!(account: account, email: email.strip.downcase)
  end

  test "customer registers and uses existing verification, login, profile, password change, and password reset flows" do
    register_and_verify_account!

    # Unknown account returns 404
    post "/api/v1/registrations",
      params: { user: { name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password" } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "nonexistent" },
      as: :json
    assert_response :not_found

    # Invalid registration params return 422 and send no email
    assert_no_emails do
      post "/api/v1/registrations",
        params: { user: { name: "  ", email: "bad-email", password: "" } },
        headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
        as: :json
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Duplicate email matching staff on same account fails
    assert_no_emails do
      post "/api/v1/registrations",
        params: { user: { name: "Jo Clone", email: "JO@ACME.TEST", password: "my-customer-password" } },
        headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },
        as: :json
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Valid customer registration ignores role/verified escalation
    assert_emails 1 do
      post "/api/v1/registrations",
        params: {
          user: {
            name: "  Avery  ",
            email: "  AVERY@EXAMPLE.TEST  ",
            password: ",
  "output_tail": "obex" },
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    acme_session = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@shared.test", password: "acme-password").dig("session", "token")
    globex_session = sign_in!(subdomain: "globex", email: "jo@shared.test", password: "globex-password").dig("session", "token")

    # Changing password on Acme does NOT revoke Globex session
    put "/api/v1/me/password",
      params: { password_change: { current_password: "acme-password", password: "new-acme-password" } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{acme_session}" },
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    get "/api/v1/me", headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "globex", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{globex_session}" }
    assert_response :ok

    # Password reset token on Acme cannot be used on Globex
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    post "/api/v1/password_resets",
      params: { password_reset: { email: "jo@shared.test" } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme" },

**Controller Parameter Handling and Timestamp Updates**

Okay, first things first, this is excellent. It confirms my initial understanding: each controller is behaving exactly as expected, reading only the parameters it understands (like `params[:status]`, etc.) and gracefully ignoring anything else, just like a well-behaved Rails API. Perfect!

Now, the crucial part: handling timestamps and sorting when updating priorities. This is the real insight here. Let's delve into the `TicketsController#update` method and the associated tests in `ticket_assignments_and_private_notes_test.rb`.

Looking at the update logic:

status_changed = ticket.will_save_change_to_status?
public_comment_added = comment.present? && comment.public?
now = Time.current

Okay, here's the breakdown:

1.  When staff updates a ticket (changing assignee, adding a private note, or—crucially—changing priority):
    *   `ticket.updated_at = now`: This is *always* updated, meaning the ticket correctly moves to the top of the staff's "recently active" list. That's good.
    *   `ticket.customer_updated_at` is ONLY updated if `status_changed || public_comment_added` is true!
    *   The "Priority is internal" concept is key here. Changing *only* the priority, or priority with assignee/private note, should *not* alter `customer_updated_at` or the customer's request order. This fits, as they are not visible to the customer.
    *   Conversely, if staff updates `priority: "high"` *and* `status: "pending"` (or adds a public comment), then `status_changed || public_comment_added` becomes true, so `customer_updated_at` *does* update!

    This aligns perfectly with the current architecture in `TicketsController#update`. No changes needed.

2.  Next, let's look at the validation in `TicketsController#update`.

    Currently, the code checks:

    has_comment = ticket_params.key?(:comment)
    has_status = ticket_params.key?(:status)
    has_assignee = ticket_params.key?(:assignee_id)

    unless has_comment || has_status || has_assignee
        return render json: {
        error: "Comment, status, or assignee is required",
        errors: { ticket: [ "must include comment, status, or assignee_id" ] }
        }, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end

    With `priority` included, it will be:

    has_comment = ticket_params.key?(:comment)
    has_status = ticket_params.key?(:status)
    has_assignee = ticket_params.key?(:assignee_id)
    has_priority = ticket_params.key?(:priority)

    unless has_comment || has_status || has_assignee || has_priority
        return render json: {
        error: "Comment, status, assignee, or priority is required",
        errors: { ticket: [ "must include comment, status, assignee_id, or priority" ] }
        }, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end

    The important thing now is to test the exact string `"Comment, status, or assignee is required"`. Need to use `grep` across the test directory to locate the exact string. This confirms that nothing is broken when we add priority.

module Api
  module V1
    class InvitationAcceptancesController < BaseController
      before_action :require_account!
      before_action :require_active_account!

      def create
        acceptance_params = require_hash_param(:invitation_acceptance)
        token = acceptance_params[:token].to_s
        now = Time.current

        user = nil

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          current_account.lock!
          invitation = current_account.invitations.find_by_token(token)

          if invitation.nil? || !invitation.pending?(now) || current_account.users.exists?(email: invitation.email)
            return render json: {
              error: "Invalid or expired invitation token",
              errors: { token: [ "is invalid or expired" ] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end

          user = current_account.users.new(
            name: acceptance_params[:name],
            email: invitation.email,
            password: acceptance_params[:password],
            role: invitation.role,
            verified_at: now
          )

          user.save!
          invitation.update!(accepted_at: now, accepted_by: user)
        end

        render json: {
          user: user.as_api_json,
          account: current_account.as_api_json
        }, status: :created
      end
    end
  end
end

**Analyzing Query Parameter Handling for Search Filters**

Okay, let's break down how we're handling search queries across `BaseController`, `InvitationsController`, and `UsersController`. First, I'm noticing the consistent approach to the `q` parameter. We start with `raw_q = params[:q]`.  Then we need to handle some specific scenarios.

If `raw_q` is `nil`, we treat it as no search filter applied, which is standard. If it's an Array or Hash (potentially malicious input, or mis-formatted), we return a `422 Unprocessable Entity` error. But, if `raw_q` is a String (or even a Symbol or Numeric, since Rails converts those query params to strings), we then apply `.to_s.strip` to it.

The `.strip` is where the core logic resides. Let's think through that carefully.  If a user searches for `"  receipt  "`, after stripping, it becomes `"receipt"`. That's a deliberate choice. Similarly, `"   "` becomes `""`, which effectively disables the search – we return an unfiltered list, and that's the intended behaviour. If the user types `"foo bar"`, we retain the internal space because `.strip` only handles leading and trailing spaces. This, and the way we deal with special characters such as `100%`, `_`, and `\`, are worth more consideration:

The key consideration is whether we *expect* leading/trailing whitespace to be preserved or stripped. The ticket subject search is a good example; by stripping spaces, we make it more inclusive, and prevent a situation where someone would search something like `"  receipt  "` and get no matches, if the search term does not match the exact input.

The other consideration is to ensure that searching for whitespace-only (e.g., `q=" "`) functions the same as an absent query, which it does. This behavior aligns with every other query parameter (`status=""`, `status="   "`, etc.).

Remember, this consistent whitespace handling is standard across the code, as seen in other normalizations.

Given that consistency and the implications of retaining or removing the spaces, I need to verify that we are correctly handling tricky characters within the search query. *   And finally, Unicode case-insensitivity – make sure the search is correctly ignoring case and accent variations.

Okay, let's really think this through... the `extract_scalar_string` method is the key. Currently, it handles `String`, `Symbol`, and `Integer`. What if someone sends a `Float`, a `Boolean`, or even an `Array` or `Hash` as a parameter? With the way Rails parses query strings, a float like `99.95` would arrive as the string `"99.95"`, which would likely pass the existing checks, but might lead to unexpected behavior. Likewise, a boolean `"true"` could be passed and would not be handled by the controller's business logic.

I need to nail down how we're handling different data types. For instance, what happens if `assignee_id` is passed as a float, `1.5`, or `true` for a boolean, `false` for a boolean. Or even if `q` is passed an array, and what about symbols?

It seems that the only non-scalar types we'll see over HTTP GET are `Array`, `Hash`, or `ActionController::Parameters`. I need to adjust `extract_scalar_string` to explicitly handle those cases and return `nil`. This is where the vulnerability exists and is critical to resolve. Now I'm considering all possibilities:

module Api
  module V1
    class BaseController < ApplicationController
      class InvalidPaginationError < StandardError
        attr_reader :errors_hash

        def initialize(message, errors_hash)
          super(message)
          @errors_hash = errors_hash
        end
      end

      DEFAULT_PAGE = 1
      DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25

      rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing, with: :render_parameter_missing
      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, with: :render_record_invalid
      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, with: :render_record_not_unique
      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound, with: :render_not_found
      rescue_from InvalidPaginationError, with: :render_invalid_pagination

      private

      attr_reader :current_account, :current_session, :current_user

      def require_hash_param(key)
        value = params.require(key)
        unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
          raise ActionController::ParameterMissing, key
        end
        value
      end

      def require_account!
        subdomain = request.headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"].to_s.strip.downcase
        @current_account = subdomain.present? ? Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain) : nil

        unless @current_account
          render json: { error: "Account not found" }, status: :not_found
        end
      end

      def authenticate_user!
        raw_token = extract_bearer_token
        @current_session = Session.authenticate_for_account(current_account, raw_token)
        @current_user = @current_session&.user

        if @current_user.nil? || @current_user.suspended?
          @current_session = nil
          @current_user = nil
          render json: { error: "Unauthorized" }, status: :unauthorized
        end
      end

      def require_active_account!
        if current_account&.cancelled?
          render json: { error: "Account is cancelled" }, status: :forbidden
        end
      end

      def require_owner!
        unless current_account&.owner?(current_user)
          render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
        end
      end

      def require_admin!
        unless current_user&.admin?
          render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
        end
      end

      def require_customer!
        unless current_user&.customer?
          render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
        end
      end

      def require_staff!
        unless current_user&.staff?
          render json: { error: "Forbidden" }, status: :forbidden
        end
      end

      def blank_filter_param?(raw)
        raw.nil? || ((raw.is_a?(String) || raw.is_a?(Symbol)) && raw.to_s.strip.empty?)
      end

      def extract_scalar_string(raw)
        return nil if raw.is_a?(Array) || raw.is_a?(Hash) || raw.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

        raw.to_s.strip
      end

      def render_paginated(collection_key, scope)
        page = parse_positive_integer_param(:page, default: DEFAULT_PAGE)
        per_page = parse_positive_integer_param(:per_page, default: DEFAULT_PER_PAGE)

        total_count = scope.count
        total_pages = total_count.zero? ? 0 : (total_count.to_f / per_page).ceil
        records = scope.offset((page - 1) * per_page).limit(per_page)

        next_page = page < total_pages ? page + 1 : nil
        previous_page = if page > 1 && total_pages > 0
          [ page - 1, total_pages ].min
        else
          nil
        end

        render json: {
          collection_key => yield(records),
          count: total_count,
          page: page,
          per_page: per_page,
          next_page: next_page,
          previous_page: previous_page
        }, status: :ok
      end

      def parse_positive_integer_param(name, default:)
        raw = params[name]
        return default if raw.nil? || raw.to_s.strip.empty?

        str = raw.to_s.strip
        unless str.match?(/\A\d+\z/)
          raise InvalidPaginationError.new(
            "#{name.to_s.humanize} must be a positive integer",
            { name => [ "must be a positive integer" ] }
          )
        end

        value = str.to_i
        if value < 1
          raise InvalidPaginationError.new(
            "#{name.to_s.humanize} must be greater than 0",
            { name => [ "must be greater than 0" ] }
          )
        end

        value
      end

      def extract_bearer_token
        header = request.headers["Authorization"].to_s
        match = header.match(/\ABearer\s+(\S+)\z/i)
        match ? match[1] : nil
      end

      def render_parameter_missing(exception)
        render json: { error: exception.message }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

      def render_record_invalid(exception)
        record = exception.record
        render json: {
          error: record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence,
          errors: record.errors.to_hash(true)
        }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

      def render_record_not_unique(_exception)
        render json: { error: "Record already exists" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

      def render_not_found(_exception)
        render json: { error: "Not found" }, status: :not_found
      end

      def render_invalid_pagination(exception)
        render json: {
          error: exception.message,
          errors: exception.errors_hash
        }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end
  end
end

    # "100%" matches t2 ("100% VAT"), NOT t3 ("1000 points")
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "100%" }, headers: owner_headers

    assert_equal [ t2 ], JSON.parse(response.body).fetch("tickets").map { |t| t.fetch("id") }

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "%" }, headers: owner_headers

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "ORDER_42" }, headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t2 ], JSON.parse(response.body).fetch("tickets").map { |t| t.fetch("id") }

    # Single trailing backslash "\" and path with trailing backslash do not crash and match literally
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "\\" }, headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t5, t3 ], JSON.parse(response.body).fetch("tickets").map { |t| t.fetch("id") }

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "c:\\users\\avery\\logs\\" }, headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t3 ], JSON.parse(response.body).fetch("tickets").map { |t| t.fetch("id") }

    # Literal "\%" matches t5 ("Literal \%"), NOT t2 ("100% VAT")
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "\\%" }, headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t5 ], JSON.parse(response.body).fetch("tickets").map { |t| t.fetch("id") }

    # Regex characters matched literally
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "[REGEX].*" }, headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t5 ], JSON.parse(response.body).fetch("tickets").map { |t| t.fetch("id") }

    # Pagination works accurately with search and filters
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "receipt", page: 1, per_page: 2 }, headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :ok
    p1 = JSON.parse(response.body)
    assert_equal [ t6, t5 ], p1.fetch("tickets").map { |t| t.fetch("id") }
    assert_equal 5, p1.fetch("count")
    assert_equal 2, p1.fetch("next_page")
    assert_nil p1.fetch("previous_page")

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "receipt", page: 3, per_page: 2 }, headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :ok
    p3 = JSON.parse(response.body)
    assert_equal [ t1 ], p3.fetch("tickets").map { |t| t.fetch("id") }
    assert_equal 5, p3.fetch("count")
    assert_nil p3.fetch("next_page")
    assert_equal 2, p3.fetch("previous_page")

    # Suspending Sam unassigns t4 while keeping its high priority -> now appears in unassigned + high + receipt!
    travel_to(base_time + 10.minutes) do
      patch "/api/v1/users/#{agent_sam.id}",
        params: { user: { suspended: true } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok

      get "/api/v1/tickets?status=open&assignee_id=unassigned&priority=high&q=receipt", headers: owner_headers
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal [ t4, t2, t1 ], JSON.parse(response.body).fetch("tickets").map { |t| t.fetch("id") }
    end

    [
      { status: "closed" },
      { status: [ "open" ] },
      { priority: "urgent" },
      { priority: [ "high" ] },
      { assignee_id: "nobody" },
      { assignee_id: "0" },
      { assignee_id: "-2" },
      { assignee_id: [ "unassigned" ] },
      { requester_id: "unassigned" },
      { requester_id: "abc" },
      { requester_id: "0" },
      { requester_id: "-5" },
      { requester_id: [ cust_avery.id.to_s ] },
      { q: [ "receipt" ] }
    ].each do |bad_params|
      get "/api/v1/tickets", params: bad_params, headers: owner_headers
      assert_response :unprocessable_entity, "Expected 422 for params=#{bad_params.inspect}"
    end

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { status: "bogus", priority: "critical" }, headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    multi_err = JSON.parse(response.body)
    assert multi_err.dig("errors", "status").present?
    assert multi_err.dig("errors", "priority").present?

  test "customers can filter their own requests by status without exposing other customers or internal priority" do
    base_time = Time.utc(2026, 11, 21, 14, 0, 0)

    _, owner = nil, nil
    avery = nil
    blake = nil

    travel_to(base_time) do
      _, owner = register_and_verify_account!(account_name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test")
      avery = register_and_verify_customer!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test")
      blake = register_and_verify_customer!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Blake", email: "blake@example.test")
    end

    owner_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password").dig("session", "token")
    avery_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password").dig("session", "token")
    blake_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "blake@example.test", password: "my-customer-password").dig("session", "token")

    owner_headers = { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{owner_token}" }
    avery_headers = { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{avery_token}" }
    blake_headers = { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "acme", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{blake_token}" }

    r_open_1 = r_pending = r_solved = r_open_2 = blake_open = nil

    travel_to(base_time + 1.minute) do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Avery Open 1", comment: { body: "First open" } } },
        headers: avery_headers,
        as: :json
      r_open_1 = JSON.parse(response.body).dig("request", "id")
    end

    travel_to(base_time + 2.minutes) do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Avery Pending", comment: { body: "Will be pending" } } },
        headers: avery_headers,
        as: :json
      r_pending = JSON.parse(response.body).dig("request", "id")
    end

    travel_to(base_time + 3.minutes) do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Avery Solved", comment: { body: "Will be solved" } } },
        headers: avery_headers,
        as: :json
      r_solved = JSON.parse(response.body).dig("request", "id")
    end

    travel_to(base_time + 4.minutes) do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Avery Open 2", comment: { body: "Second open" } } },
        headers: avery_headers,
        as: :json
      r_open_2 = JSON.parse(response.body).dig("request", "id")
    end

    travel_to(base_time + 5.minutes) do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Blake Open", comment: { body: "Other customer open" } } },
        headers: blake_headers,
        as: :json
      blake_open = JSON.parse(response.body).dig("request", "id")
      assert_not_nil blake_open
    end

    # Staff sets r_pending to pending, r_solved to solved, and marks r_open_1 high priority internally
    travel_to(base_time + 6.minutes) do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{r_pending}",
        params: { ticket: { status: "pending" } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok

      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{r_solved}",
        params: { ticket: { status: "solved" } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok

      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{r_open_1}",
        params: { ticket: { priority: "high" } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    # Filter Avery's requests by each status (note r_open_2 is still newer in customer_updated_at than r_open_1!)
    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "open" }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    open_res = JSON.parse(response.body)
    assert_equal [ r_open_2, r_open_1 ], open_res.fetch("requests").map { |r| r.fetch("id") }
    assert_equal 2, open_res.fetch("count")
    assert open_res.fetch("requests").none? { |r| r.key?("priority") }

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "  PENDING " }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ r_pending ], JSON.parse(response.body).fetch("requests").map { |r| r.fetch("id") }

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "SOLVED" }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ r_solved ], JSON.parse(response.body).fetch("requests").map { |r| r.fetch("id") }

    # Blank status returns all of Avery's requests ordered by customer_updated_at desc
    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "   " }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ r_solved, r_pending, r_open_2, r_open_1 ], JSON.parse(response.body).fetch("requests").map { |r| r.fetch("id") }

    # Pagination combined with status filter
    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "open", page: 1, per_page: 1 }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    open_p1 = JSON.parse(response.body)
    assert_equal [ r_open_2 ], open_p1.fetch("requests").map { |r| r.fetch("id") }
    assert_equal 2, open_p1.fetch("count")
    assert_equal 2, open_p1.fetch("next_page")

    # Passing priority or requester_id on GET /requests is ignored (cannot probe internal priority or other customers)
    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "open", priority: "high", requester_id: blake.id }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ r_open_2, r_open_1 ], JSON.parse(response.body).fetch("requests").map { |r| r.fetch("id") }

    # Invalid status filter on GET /requests returns 422
    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "archived" }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert JSON.parse(response.body).dig("errors", "status").present?

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: [ "open" ] }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Customers still cannot access staff /tickets even with filters
    get "/api/v1/tickets?status=open&priority=high", headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :forbidden
  end
end

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :assigned_tickets, optional: true
  has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :status, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }
  normalizes :priority, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  before_validation :ensure_customer_updated_at, on: :create

  validates :subject, presence: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_is_assignable_staff

  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :customer_recently_active, -> { order(customer_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :matching_query, ->(query) {
    return none if query.to_s.include?("\u0000")

    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(query.to_s, "\\")}%"
    where(
      <<~SQL.squish,
        tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\\'
        OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM comments
          WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id
            AND comments.account_id = tickets.account_id
            AND comments.public = TRUE
            AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\\'
        )
      SQL
      pattern: pattern
    )
  }

  def as_request_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: customer_updated_at
    }
  end

  def as_ticket_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      priority: priority,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      requester: requester.as_requester_json,
      assignee_id: assignee_id,
      assignee: assignee&.as_assignee_json,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def ensure_customer_updated_at
    if customer_updated_at.nil?
      now = Time.current
      self.created_at ||= now
      self.updated_at ||= now
      self.customer_updated_at = self.updated_at
    end
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    if account_id.present? && requester.present? && requester.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:requester, :invalid)
    end
  end

  def assignee_is_assignable_staff
    return if assignee_id.nil? && assignee.nil?

    if assignee.nil? || (account_id.present? && assignee.account_id != account_id) || !assignee.staff? || assignee.suspended?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, :invalid)
    end
  end
end

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :assigned_tickets, optional: true
  has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :status, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }
  normalizes :priority, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  before_validation :ensure_customer_updated_at, on: :create

  validates :subject, presence: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_is_assignable_staff

  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :customer_recently_active, -> { order(customer_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :matching_query, ->(query) {
    return none if query.to_s.include?("\u0000")

    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(query.to_s, "\\")}%"
    where(
      <<~SQL.squish,
        tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\\'
        OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM comments
          WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id
            AND comments.account_id = tickets.account_id
            AND comments.public = TRUE
            AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\\'
        )
      SQL
      pattern: pattern
    )
  }

  def as_request_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: customer_updated_at
    }
  end

  def as_ticket_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      priority: priority,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      requester: requester.as_requester_json,
      assignee_id: assignee_id,
      assignee: assignee&.as_assignee_json,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def ensure_customer_updated_at
    if customer_updated_at.nil?
      now = Time.current
      self.created_at ||= now
      self.updated_at ||= now
      self.customer_updated_at = self.updated_at
    end
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    if account_id.present? && requester.present? && requester.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:requester, :invalid)
    end
  end

  def assignee_is_assignable_staff
    return if assignee_id.nil? && assignee.nil?

    if assignee.nil? || (account_id.present? && assignee.account_id != account_id) || !assignee.staff? || assignee.suspended?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, :invalid)
    end
  end
end

I have implemented ticket priorities, combined ticket filtering and literal search for staff, and status filtering for customer requests:

1. **Ticket Priority (`normal` | `high`)**:
   - Added `priority` (`null: false, default: "normal"`) to `tickets` along with indexes in `db/migrate/20261121000004_add_priority_to_tickets.rb`.
   - Added normalization, validation (`Ticket::PRIORITIES = %w[normal high]`), and `priority` serialization to staff `Ticket#as_ticket_json`, while keeping `priority` internal and excluded from customer `Ticket#as_request_json`, customer creation/updates, and `customer_updated_at` activity tracking.
   - Updated `Api::V1::TicketsController#update` so staff can update `priority` (alone or alongside `status`, `assignee_id`, and `comment`).

2. **Staff Ticket Filtering & Literal Search (`GET /api/v1/tickets`)**:
   - Added combinable filters for `status`, `priority`, `assignee_id` (positive integer ID or `unassigned`), `requester_id` (positive integer ID), and `q` (case-insensitive literal substring search across ticket subjects and public comments, safely escaping `%`, `_`, and `\` via `sanitize_sql_like` + `ILIKE ... ESCAPE '\'`).
   - Invalid filter values return `422 Unprocessable Entity` with structured `error` and `errors`.

3. **Customer Request Status Filtering (`GET /api/v1/requests`)**:
   - Added `status` filtering for a customer's own requests while keeping internal fields (`priority`, `assignee_id`, private notes) isolated.

4. **Tests**:
   - Added integration tests in `test/integration/ticket_priorities_and_filtering_test.rb` and verified the full CI suite (`bin/ci`).
